recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Thousands of galaxies fill this view, some belonging to the Coma Cluster itself and others lying far behind it. The image was taken with the Dark Energy Camera. The cluster takes its name from the hair of the Egyptian queen Berenice II, a figure who also appears in Greek mythology, and it lies about 320 million light-years away.

The Coma Cluster was fundamental to the discovery of dark matter. In 1937, the Swiss astronomer Fritz Zwicky noticed that its galaxies behaved as though huge quantities of matter were pulling on them, matter that could not be seen. That unseen material is what we now call dark matter.

A galaxy cluster is a huge collection of galaxies bound together by gravity. The speeds of the galaxies inside it reveal how much mass is holding the cluster together, and in Coma that mass far exceeds what the visible galaxies account for.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (52.96 x 33.54 arcminutes) and distance (320 million light yearsz=0.023 (redshift)), the frame spans roughly 4.9 million × 3.1 million light-years. Its light set out about 320 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: The Dark Energy Camera on the Blanco 4-meter Telescope observed the Coma Cluster through g, r, i and z filters, covering visible and near-infrared light. The colours assigned to each filter are not published.
